ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #5 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which phrase is a better word for 'nice' food? (1 mark)
   A. cold
   B. bad
   C. hard
   D. delicious

2. Which sentence would be a good first sentence? (1 mark)
   A. On Saturday, Mama took me to the supermarket.
   B. The end.
   C. Yours lovingly.
   D. Thank you.

3. An email is (1 mark)
   A. a type of phone
   B. a message sent electronically
   C. a letter sent by bus
   D. a kind of paper

4. In the email dialogue, which button did they click first to write a new message? (1 mark)
   A. Reply
   B. Save
   C. Compose
   D. Send

5. Dialogues: Which question is inferential? (1 mark)
   A. Which button did they click?
   B. How do you think Baraka felt at the end?
   C. Where do they see the reply?
   D. Who wrote the address?

6. Which word fits: 'Do you have ___ pencils?' (1 mark)
   A. some
   B. much
   C. any
   D. a lot

7. Which sentence shows a habit in the present tense? (1 mark)
   A. I asked my mother yesterday.
   B. I had asked my mother.
   C. I always ask my mother before opening a new page.
   D. I was asking my mother.

8. Which word means 'free time when you rest or play'? (1 mark)
   A. crime
   B. trust
   C. leisure
   D. laptop

9. Which helping verb completes: 'They ____ watching TV when the power went off.'? (1 mark)
   A. was
   B. is
   C. am
   D. were

10. Which sentence shows two actions going on at the same time in the past? (1 mark)
   A. I have cooked while she washed.
   B. I cooked and my sister washes plates.
   C. I am cooking and my sister was washing plates.
   D. I was cooking while my sister was washing plates.

11. Which of these does NOT need a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. Christmas
   B. Madaraka Day
   C. dry season
   D. Eid

12. Which word has the vowel glide /ʊə/? (1 mark)
   A. maize
   B. plough
   C. harvest
   D. manure

13. Which is a good strategy for improving fluency? (1 mark)
   A. Skipping hard words
   B. Reading only the pictures
   C. Re-reading the same passage several times
   D. Reading each word very slowly with long stops

14. What should you do at a full stop when reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Skip the next word
   B. Pause a little
   C. Shout
   D. Speed up

15. Which is the correct negative of 'He works on the farm'? (1 mark)
   A. He doesn't works on the farm.
   B. He don't work on the farm.
   C. He doesn't work on the farm.
   D. He isn't work on the farm.

16. What does 'prevention' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Acting so that something bad does not happen
   B. Medicine that cures an illness
   C. A kind of food
   D. A sharp object

17. Which word in the story means 'said no to doing something'? (1 mark)
   A. refused
   B. noticed
   C. nodded
   D. smiled

18. What did Baraka do that showed he was a good friend? (1 mark)
   A. He told the others to stay away
   B. He ran away
   C. He laughed at Omondi
   D. He explained the facts and invited Omondi to play

19. Which end mark is right for: 'How many books have you read'? (1 mark)
   A. ?
   B. .
   C. !
   D. ,

20. Which sentence has a comma used correctly before 'but'? (1 mark)
   A. I, wanted to go but it was raining.
   B. I wanted to go but, it was raining.
   C. I wanted, to go but it was raining.
   D. I wanted to go, but it was raining.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Put in order: Baraka presses Send; Achieng explains what an email is; they click Compose. (3 marks)

22. Write a short dialogue of four lines between two learners about sending an email. (4 marks)

23. Write the -ing form of each verb: make, run, play, lie. (4 marks)

24. Change to the past progressive: 'The children are singing in the hall.' (2 marks)

25. Give the meaning of each word and use it in a sentence: (a) harvest (b) fertilizer. (4 marks)

26. Explain why 'She asked where the clinic was?' is wrong and correct it. (3 marks)

27. Write two polite phrases you could use in a conversation, one to add something and one to give the other person a turn. (2 marks)

28. Explain what the proverb 'Many hands make light work' means and give an example. (3 marks)

29. List three things you can do to remember what you have read. (3 marks)

30. Correct: (a) 'How much books are there?' (b) 'I do not have some money.' (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #5 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — delicious
   Delicious is a stronger, more exact word.

2. A — On Saturday, Mama took me to the supermarket.
   It tells when, who and where.

3. B — a message sent electronically
   Email stands for electronic mail.

4. C — Compose
   They clicked Compose.

5. B — How do you think Baraka felt at the end?
   You must work it out from clues.

6. C — any
   Any is used in questions with plural nouns.

7. C — I always ask my mother before opening a new page.
   'Always' and the simple present 'ask' show a habit.

8. C — leisure
   Leisure is free time.

9. D — were
   'They' takes 'were' in the past progressive.

10. D — I was cooking while my sister was washing plates.
   'While' links two past progressive actions.

11. C — dry season
   Seasons are common nouns and take small letters.

12. D — manure
   'Manure' has the /ʊə/ sound, as in 'pure'.

13. C — Re-reading the same passage several times
   Each re-reading improves speed and expression.

14. B — Pause a little
   A full stop tells the reader to pause.

15. C — He doesn't work on the farm.
   After doesn't, the verb returns to its base form.

16. A — Acting so that something bad does not happen
   Prevention stops problems before they start.

17. A — refused
   Some children refused to play with Omondi.

18. D — He explained the facts and invited Omondi to play
   Baraka used facts to help.

19. A — ?
   It is a direct question.

20. D — I wanted to go, but it was raining.
   A comma comes before but when joining two full sentences.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Achieng explains what an email is; they click Compose; Baraka presses Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct position.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: A: How do we send an email? B: First click Compose. A: Now I type the address. B: Then write your message and press Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each line with correct speaker format.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: making, running, playing, lying
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct spelling.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: The children were singing in the hall.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for were, 1 mark for keeping singing.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) Harvest: to gather crops that are ready. We harvest maize in August. (b) Fertilizer: something added to soil to help plants grow. The farmer put fertilizer on the field.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each word: 1 for the meaning and 1 for a correct sentence.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: It reports a question, so it is a statement and needs a full stop. Correct: She asked where the clinic was.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reason, 1 for correction, 1 for full stop.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: 'May I add something?' and 'What do you think?'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable polite phrase.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: It means a job is easier when many people help. For example, the whole class can sweep the compound quickly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 1 for a suitable example, 1 for clear expression.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Write new words and meanings; say one sentence about each chapter; draw a story map; retell the story to a partner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct suggestion.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) How many books are there? (b) I do not have any money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
